candidates.decision_relevance: Would help distinguish persistent participation deterioration or recovery from noisy endpoint readings and breadth snapshots with changing constituent membership.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews repeatedly report conflicting proxy breadth readings, different point-in-time membership hashes, and no comparable breadth trend (for example, 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-02 outputs).
candidates.metric_name: Fixed-universe constituent returns and advancer/decliner counts
candidates.missing_history_problem: A timestamped constituent-level history for a consistently defined universe is not supplied; the available breadth snapshots cannot establish whether participation changes persisted.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would show whether positive or negative ETF evidence persisted or reversed across sessions, rather than relying on isolated settled observations.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews repeatedly describe ETF evidence as one settled session and insufficient to establish a flow trend; weekly reviews also note that flow timing relative to deterioration is unclear.
candidates.metric_name: Daily settled BTC and ETH ETF net flows
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied analyses include isolated settled sessions but no aligned multi-session history with settlement dates, preventing assessment of persistence and sequencing against price and breadth changes.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would clarify the order and duration of price moves and deterioration across short horizons, reducing ambiguity from unavailable hourly anchors and nominal windows with shorter actual spans.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly report unavailable 1-hour horizons, anchor-tolerance violations, and API windows whose actual spans are shorter than their labels; weekly reviews also identify missing event-time alignment.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped hourly BTC, ETH, and ETH/BTC price series
candidates.missing_history_problem: A continuous, timestamp-aligned hourly sequence suitable for consistent realized-window calculations is not supplied, limiting path and event-sequence comparisons across analyses.
